answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a zephyr as the anchor of the cost.
